newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA ELECTION MONITORS SAY POLL NOT FREE OR FAIR.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA ELECTION MONITORS SAY POLL NOT FREE OR FAIR.

text.p: Independent election monitors said on Wednesday that this week's Zambian elections were neither free nor fair.

The Committee for a Clean Campaign, an umbrella group of 19 non-governmental and civic organisations which monitored the polls, said voting took place in a free and fair atmosphere, but the run-up to the elections was designed to give the ruling party an unfair advantage.

The committee said in a statement that flawed voter registration, abuses of government resources and partisan state-run media had favoured President Frederick Chiluba's Movement for Multi-party Democracy.
"In view of all this, the 1996 presidential and parliamentary elections can not be said to have been free and fair," the statement said.
Chiluba and his party were headed for a landslide victory in the polls which took place on Monday as results trickled in.
Most opposition parties, including "Father of the Nation" Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party, boycotted the voting and have said they will not recognise the results.
